title: Active Alignment Dominance in Three-Fibre Coherence Recovery
abstract: Within a three-fibre toy architecture modelling the leakage-alignment structure of the Q5 transport framework, active re-alignment after phase disturbance produces substantially higher coherence recovery than passive evolution under the unmodified generator. The toy-model program is introduced as a structural stress test of the leakage-alignment architecture, not as a claim of physical realization. The three-fibre space \( span{u_2, u_3, u_4} \) implements the Q5 leakage sector structure (T124, T127): outer fibres u_2 and u_4 carry coherent transport and are coupled only through the middle fibre u_3, which acts as a mandatory balancing channel. Phase disturbances are applied to the first outer fibre via \( ψ_φ = (1/√3)(e^{iφ}, 1, 1) \) , with recovery quality measured by fidelity \( F(t) = |⟨ψ_align, ψ(t)⟩|² \). Key numerical results (tested sweep): Moderate disturbance (φ = π/2): passive recovery F_max ≈ 0.623; active re-alignment F_max ≈ 0.916. Middle fibre strongly recruited. Hard inversion (φ = π): passive recovery F_max ≈ 0.180; active re-alignment F_max ≈ 0.731. Passive reconstruction strongly suppressed. Broad state family (60 asymmetric initial states): re-alignment outperformed passive recovery on maximum fidelity in 98.33% of cases at φ = π/2 and 96.67% at φ = π; on mean fidelity in 100% of cases in both regimes. Three corollaries are established: effective irreversibility under restricted return (recovery requires information, not time); information- demanding reversibility (recovery quality scales with protocol information content); and a balancing-to-rupture regime split with crossover near φ_c ~ 0.7π–0.8π, not yet proven universal. The theorem proves that within the tested architecture, coherence behaves as an actively maintained alignment condition rather than a passively self-restoring property. No claim is made about physical laboratory decoherence, quantum error correction, or gravitational stabilization.

title: Symmetries Here and There, Combined Everywhere: Cross-space Symmetry Compositions in Robotics
abstract: Robots exhibit a rich variety of symmetries arising from their mechanical structure and the properties of their tasks. Although many robotics problems exhibit several symmetries simultaneously, existing approaches typically treat them in isolation, failing to exploit their combined potential. This paper introduces cross-space symmetry compositions, a framework for learning robot policies that are jointly equivariant to multiple symmetries across configuration and task spaces. Leveraging the differential-geometric structure of the forward kinematics map, we both descend symmetries from configuration to task space and lift symmetries from task to configuration space, enabling their composition within a unified representation space. We validate our framework on simulated and real-world experiments on a dual-arm robot, demonstrating that jointly leveraging multiple symmetries yields improved generalization. Video and source code are available at https://sites.google.com/view/cross-space-symmetries.

title: SpaceDG: Benchmarking Spatial Intelligence under Visual Degradation
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in spatial intelligence, yet existing spatial reasoning benchmarks largely assume pristine visual inputs and overlook the degradations that commonly occur in real-world deployment, such as motion blur, low light, adverse weather, lens distortion, and compression artifacts. This raises a fundamental question: how robust is the spatial intelligence of current MLLMs when visual observations are imperfect? To answer this question, we introduce SpaceDG, the first large-scale dataset for degradation-aware spatial understanding. It is constructed with a physically grounded degradation synthesis engine that embeds degradation formation process into 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) rendering, enabling realistic simulation of nine degradation types. The resulting dataset contains approximately 1M QA pairs from nearly 1,000 indoor scenes. We further introduce SpaceDG-Bench, an human-verified benchmark with 1,102 questions spanning 11 reasoning categories and 9 visual degradation types, yielding over 10K VQA instances. Evaluating 25 open- and closed-source MLLMs reveals that visual degradations consistently and substantially impair spatial reasoning, exposing a critical robustness gap. Finally, we show that finetuning on SpaceDG markedly improves degradation robustness and can even surpass human performance under degraded conditions without any performance drop on clean images, highlighting the promise of degradation-aware training for robust spatial intelligence.

title: Toward Understanding Adversarial Distillation: Why Robust Teachers Fail
abstract: Adversarial Distillation aims to enhance student robustness by guiding the student with a robust teacher's soft labels within the min-max adversarial training framework, yet its success is notoriously inconsistent: a more robust teacher often fails to improve, or even harms, the student's robust generalization. In this paper, we identify a key mechanism of this teacher dependency: the misalignment between the teacher's supervisory confidence and the student's representational limitations on a consistent subset of training data -- the Robustly Unlearnable Set. We present a theoretical framework analyzing the feature learning dynamics of a two-layer neural network, demonstrating that this mismatch creates a dichotomy in distillation outcomes. We prove that when a teacher provides confident supervision on unlearnable samples, it compels the student to memorize spurious noise patterns that eventually overpower the learned robust signal, thereby driving robust overfitting. Conversely, a teacher that exhibits high uncertainty on these samples effectively suppresses noise memorization, allowing the student to rely solely on the learnable signal for robust generalization. We empirically validate our theory across both synthetic simulations and real-image classification datasets, confirming that robust overfitting is driven by the teacher's interaction with unlearnable samples. Finally, we demonstrate that a teacher's predictive entropy on unlearnable samples serves as a strong indicator of student robustness, validating our theoretical framework and offering a principled guideline for robust teacher selection.

title: Survival Prediction from Longitudinal Health Records: A Comparative Study of Cox, XGBoost, Transformer, and Pretrained Representations
abstract: Predicting disease progression from longitudinal health records is a key challenge in clinical data science. Traditional models such as the Cox proportional hazards model provide strong baselines but are limited in capturing nonlinear relationships and temporal dependencies. In this thesis, Finnish registry data from the FinnGen study are used to compare four approaches to disease progression prediction: a Cox model, an XGBoost survival model, a transformer-based model, and pretrained DelFI representations. Patient histories are modelled as sequences of clinical events with timestamps together with baseline covariates. The results show that richer longitudinal representations do not automatically lead to better predictive performance. Instead, improvements depend on how well the model and input representation are matched to the disease progression task. These findings highlight both the potential and the limitations of applying modern machine learning models that use longitudinal patient histories to clinical survival prediction.

title: Perspectivas de disponibilitat de recursos minerals crítics al territori Pirinenc i Prepirinec català
abstract: The Catalan Pyrenees and Pre-Pyrenees constitute one of the most geologically diverse regions of Catalonia, a feature that has historically favoured the development of numerous mining operations. However, most of these areas are currently largely inactive, mainly due to the lack of modern investigations and the environmental constraints associated with extractive activities. Despite this, the current European context, characterised by the need to reduce external dependence on critical raw materials (CRMs), has driven new initiatives aimed at the exploration and reassessment of strategic mineral resources within European territory. In this context, the present work aims to study several mineralisations from the Catalan Pyrenees and Pre-Pyrenees in order to evaluate their potential in terms of critical and strategic raw materials, as well as to establish a basis for future, more detailed investigations. The methodology combines bibliographic review, fieldwork, geochemical analyses using X-ray fluorescence, and mineralogical studies using optical microscopy and electron microscopy. This results also allow for the reinterpretation of historical mining sites from the current perspective of CRMs, showing that many deposits traditionally exploited for conventional metals may hold significantly greater strategic interest than previously considered. The results obtained have enabled the identification of significant geochemical anomalies of tungsten, molybdenum, cobalt, manganese, nickel, bismuth, antimony, light rare earth elements, silver, and gold across all studied areas. Among these, the outcrops of Port de Salau are particularly noteworthy, where very high tungsten concentrations associated with scheelite have been detected, with maximum values of up to 1.56% W, as well as significant anomalies of gold, arsenic, and bismuth related to late hydrothermal processes. In the Costabona area, particularly at the Roca del Turó mine, high tungsten concentrations have also been identified, with maxima of 1.37% W, together with notable molybdenum contents associated with molybdenite. Regarding polymetallic mineralisations, the Ferreres mine stands out due to its high copper and barium concentrations, with maximum values of 14.42% Cu and 2.23% Ba, mainly associated with chalcopyrite, tetrahedrite-tennantite, and barite, as well as the presence of relevant elements such as antimony, arsenic, and silver. On the other hand, the mines of Tossa d’Alp show significant manganese enrichment, with maximum values of 64.4% Mn mainly associated with pyrolusite, as well as cobalt and nickel anomalies linked to iron-manganese oxides. Finally, in the areas of Aós de Civís, Bordes de Conflent, and Civís, notable cobalt concentrations are observed, with maximum values of up to 0.27% Co, as well as light rare earth element anomalies associated with hydrothermal ferruginous mineralisations. Overall, the results demonstrate that the Catalan Pyrenees and Pre-Pyrenees present significant geological potential regarding several critical and strategic raw materials. Although the data obtained correspond mainly to spot samples and some results require verification through more precise analytical techniques, the detected anomalies clearly justify the need for further detailed geochemical, mineralogical, and metallogenic investigations. This work highlights the importance of re-evaluating historical mineralisations in the Catalan Pyrenees within the current context of increasing demand for critical mineral resources.

title: Рақамлаштириш ва сунъий интеллект технологияларининг ахборот-таҳлил фаолиятидаги мазмун-моҳияти.
abstract: Мазкур мақолада ички ишлар органларида ахборот-таҳлил фаолиятини рақамлаштириш ва сунъий интеллект технологияларидан фойдаланиш тизимларини жорий этишнинг назарий асослари, аҳамияти ва ўзига хос хусусиятлари ёритиб берилган. Тошкент вилояти мисолида мазкур тизимларни амалиётга татбиқ этишнинг долзарблиги асослаб берилган. Тадқиқотда рақамлаштириш ва сунъий интеллект тушунчаларининг мазмун-моҳияти таҳлил қилинган, хорижий мамлакатлар тажрибаси кўриб чиқилган ҳамда амалий тавсиялар ишлаб чиқилган
